I can prove two new results: a bound for actual irregular demand in the full source class, and the reserve inequality for every finite rotor-only fusion, with arbitrary phases and orientations. I have not proved or disproved either unrestricted joint inequality when all U phases and marked positive sides are allowed.The strongest restricted conclusion is
$$\boxed{\text{Rotor-only:}\qquad
K_{\mathrm{irregular}}\le S+C-2c_- ,}
\tag{R}$$
where  $c_-$  counts certain contact components of the negative rotors, defined below. If every rotor is negative, equality holds.The general result is
$$\boxed{
K_{\mathrm{irregular}}
\le S-H+C+\left\lfloor\frac{B_*}{2}\right\rfloor
\le S+C+\left\lfloor\frac{B_R}{2}\right\rfloor .
}
\tag{T}$$
Here  $H=B_{11}$ , and  $B_R$  counts a specific actual full-tile contact, rather than potential source slots: a new full tile whose original owners contribute a regular three-endpoint group from a zero-charge rotor and an irregular singleton.These results address the credit issue directly. The proof of (T) subtracts each tile’s regular expenditure before using its residual credit. The proof of (R) shows that dense irregular contacts force distinct full tiles through complete-support feasibility, and then pays the excess by an exact Euler identity.I use your supplied phase catalogue, regular-tile theorem, positive-side rotor barrier, and reference ledger as inputs. The arguments below do not require pair-feasibility or final occupied degree three.1. A general local bound for actual irregular eventsFor each physical tile  $Q$ , write
$$i_Q=\#\{(j,p):p\in I_j\cap Q\},$$
counting all original irregular-capable endpoints in that tile, including inactive ones. Original ownership is retained.Also set
$$C_Q=2J_Q-K_{\mathrm{regular},Q}.$$
The supplied regular-tile theorem gives  $C_Q\ge0$ , and
$$\sum_Q C_Q=C.$$
Call  $Q$  exceptional when all three conditions hold: $Q$  is a new mixed-owner full endpoint tile.Its original endpoint-owner partition is  $3+1$ .The singleton owner’s original receiver profile is  $1P1T$ .Let  $b_Q\in\{0,1\}$  be this indicator and put
$$B_*=\sum_Q b_Q.$$
Theorem 1 — Local actual-demand boundEvery feasible complete-source fusion in the stated full U/rotor class satisfies
$$\boxed{
2\bigl(K_{\mathrm{irregular},Q}-C_Q\bigr)
\le i_Q+b_Q
}
\tag{1}$$
for every physical tile  $Q$ .The exceptional term is needed in exactly one full-tile owner partition.Proof: nonfull tilesThe accepted regular-tile theorem implies
$$K_{\mathrm{regular},Q}=J_Q=C_Q=0$$
whenever  $Q$  is not full.An event requires at least two final endpoints. We examine the two possibilities.Two final endpointsSuppose  $p\to q$  is an event, with  $p,q$  adjacent. Denote the other intratile neighbor of  $p$  by  $r$ , and the fourth corner by  $s$ .The unique original blank neighbor of  $p$  is  $q$ . Therefore  $r$  was originally occupied by the owner of  $p$ . Since  $r$  is not a final endpoint, it is an original selection that remains selected. Its persistent anchor is  $p$ .Consequently,  $s$  must be finally blank: otherwise the retained selection  $r$  would have occupied neighbors  $p$  and  $s$ .Now consider the original owner of  $q$ . Final blankness of  $s$ , together with persistence of every original occupied site, makes  $s$  originally blank for that owner. Original occupied degree three then forces its other intratile neighbor  $p$  to have been originally occupied. Because  $p$  belongs to a different original endpoint owner, it was an original selection of the owner of  $q$ .Thus both original receiver profiles are  $1P1T$ . Exactly one event fires:
$$i_Q=2,\qquad K_{\mathrm{irregular},Q}=1.$$
This gives equality in (1).The retained support  $r$  is essential here. Discarding it would invalidate the conclusion.Three final endpointsThe three endpoints form an L. Its missing corner must be finally blank, since a retained selection there would see two endpoints.Each leaf of the L has that blank corner as an intratile neighbor. It is therefore the leaf’s unique original blank neighbor. Neither leaf can fire an event toward the elbow.Only the elbow can fire, and it has at most one event. If it fires, all three endpoints are irregular-capable:For a  $2+1$  owner partition, the pair has profile  $2P0T$ , and the singleton has profile  $1P1T$ .For a  $1+1+1$  partition, each leaf has the elbow as an original selected neighbor, while the firing elbow has one original selected intratile neighbor and one original blank intratile neighbor.Hence, whenever an event occurs,
$$i_Q=3,\qquad K_{\mathrm{irregular},Q}=1.$$
Inequality (1) follows, with one unit left over.Tiles with no events satisfy (1) immediately.Proof: full tilesAn original full  $4P$  tile has no new intratile event and no mixed-owner correction. All quantities in (1) vanish.For a new mixed full tile, the supplied receiver catalogue allows the following exhaustive owner partitions.Owner partitionParameters $K_{\mathrm{regular},Q}$  $K_{\mathrm{irregular},Q}$  $i_Q$  $C_Q$  $3+1$ , regular singleton— $2$  $0$  $0$  $0$  $3+1$ , irregular singleton— $2$  $1$  $1$  $0$  $2+2$  $a=$  number of irregular pairs $2-a$  $2a$  $2a$  $a$  $2+1+1$  $a\in\{0,1\}$ : pair irregular;  $q=$  irregular singletons $1-a$  $2a+q$  $2a+q$  $1+a$  $1+1+1+1$  $q=$  irregular singletons $0$  $q$  $q$  $2$ For  $3+1$ , the three-endpoint group has exactly two regular events. If the singleton is irregular, its one intratile blank is filled, so it contributes one irregular event. This is precisely the exceptional case:
$$2(K_{\mathrm{irregular},Q}-C_Q)=2=i_Q+b_Q.$$
For  $2+2$ ,
$$2(K_{\mathrm{irregular},Q}-C_Q)=2a=i_Q.$$
For  $2+1+1$ , the difference between the right and left sides of (1) is

This proves (1). Every event, original irregular slot, and correction unit has been assigned to its own physical tile exactly once. ∎2. Summation: the remaining event obstruction is very specificYour complete phase catalogue gives the exact identity

Summing (1) and using integrality gives

Split the exceptional tiles according to the original owner of the three-endpoint group:

All nonpositive U phases, with negative rotors and phase- $(1,1)$  zero rotors.Allow arbitrary phase- $(0,1)$ ,  $(1,0)$ , and  $(1,1)$  U sources, arbitrary negative rotors, and arbitrary phase- $(1,1)$  zero rotors. Then

so

Reserve for every arbitrary-phase rotor-only fusionThe preceding local theorem leaves exceptional zero-rotor contacts as a possible obstruction. In a finite rotor-only fusion, complete supports exclude those contacts—and more.Theorem 2 — Arbitrary-phase rotor reserveSuppose every original source is an affine image of the complete rotor. Both chiralities and all effective phases are allowed.Form a graph whose vertices are the charge- $-2$  rotors. Join two when the indices of their central full tiles differ by  $(\pm1,\pm1)$ . Let  $c_-$  be its number of connected components, with  $c_-=0$  if there are no negative rotors.Then
$$\boxed{
S+C-K_{\mathrm{irregular}}\ge2c_-.
}
\tag{8}$$
Since  $N=G=0$ , this proves reserve and, through your ledger,
$$\boxed{\sigma\ge2c_-.}
\tag{9}$$
If every rotor is negative, equality holds in (8).The main geometric step is a finite-completion obstruction.3.1 Exhausting all possible rotor owners of a specified siteLet
$$E=\{(1,2),(2,2),(2,3),(2,4),(3,1),(3,2),(3,3),(4,3)\},$$
and use the complete eight-selection set supplied in the question.Write  $R_+(a,b)$  for the standard rotor translated by  $(a,b)$ , and  $R_-(a,b)$  for its column reflection followed by that translation:
$$(r,c)\longmapsto(r+a,-c+b).$$
Quarter-turn invariance means that every affine rotor image belongs to one of these two translation families.For a specified endpoint  $z$ , choosing its chirality and original role  $e\in E$  determines its translation uniquely:
$$(a,b)=z-(e_r,\pm e_c).
\tag{10}$$
There are exactly sixteen roles to check. Consequently, the classifications below cover every translation, without a positional bound.Normalize a negative rotor to  $R_+(0,0)$ , and consider its irregular endpoint
$$p=(1,2),\qquad \delta(p)=(1,3).$$
Substitution in (10) shows that the only rotor owners of  $(1,3)$  whose endpoint sets avoid those of  $R_+(0,0)$  are
$$R_+(-2,2),\qquad R_+(-3,0),\qquad R_-(-3,6).
\tag{11}$$
The first is a negative rotor diagonally adjacent to the original central tile. The other two cannot occur in a finite feasible rotor fusion.3.2 Forbidden pair ASuppose the fusion contains
$$R_+(0,0),\qquad R_+(-3,0).$$
The old support  $(1,1)$  has the two persistent endpoint neighbors
$$(0,1),\qquad(1,2).$$
It must therefore be consumed by an original endpoint.The following table records all possible owners, using the same sixteen-role calculation (10).Existing sourcesForced old supportPersistent endpoint neighborsAll endpoint-disjoint rotor owners $R_+(0,0),R_+(-3,0)$  $(1,1)$  $(0,1),(1,2)$  $R_+(-1,-3)$  or  $R_-(-2,2)$ Previous pair and  $R_-(-2,2)$  $(2,1)$  $(1,1),(2,2),(3,1)$ NoneOriginal pair and  $R_+(-1,-3)$  $(0,0)$  $(0,-1),(0,1),(1,0)$  $R_+(-4,-3)$ The reflected alternative is impossible because its next forced support has no rotor endpoint owner.Thus the fusion must contain

Complete supports force the contact components to fill their cavitiesRepresent each negative rotor by the index of its central full tile.A negative rotor contributes one port endpoint to each cardinally adjacent physical tile. Every finite connected component with this property is a Cartesian rectangle:Start with a single occupied vertex.Traverse a connected ordering of the component.Whenever the next vertex extends an occupied rectangle along one side, square completion propagates the new row or column across that side.Thus the component’s growing bounding rectangle remains occupied.Every component is monochiral. Write its dimensions as  $a_h\times b_h$ , and define
$$V_-=\sum_h a_hb_h,$$

$$E_-=\sum_h\bigl((a_h-1)b_h+a_h(b_h-1)\bigr),$$

Then
$$V_--E_-+F_-=c_-.
\tag{12}$$

$$K_{\mathrm{irregular}}=2E_-.
\tag{13}$$
Every elementary rectangle face supplies a distinct physical tile with four port endpoints from four negative rotors. It is a new mixed full tile. It must itself be consumed by another original endpoint.This identifies where the larger problem resumes: U sources may terminate or redirect the forced rotor-support chains, but their further support obligations and marked-side costs still need a single-use payment argument.The established conclusions are therefore:Full source class: the actual-demand bound (3)–(4), isolating the exceptional  $3+1$  contacts.The U/rotor subclasses in Section 2: automatic reserve without the previous density condition.Every finite arbitrary-phase rotor-only fusion: the stronger reserve theorem  $S+C-K_{\mathrm{irregular}}\ge2c_-$ , with exact all-parameter examples.Unrestricted mixed U/rotor class with marked positive sides: both requested universal inequalities remain unresolved, and no complete feasible counterexample is claimed.
